subject: tu:game/enemy/enemy
value:
THE FULL FLIP AUDIT FOR game/enemy/enemy.c, run at commit 6670e3ab4. v1 reported only the text half. The work order treats the flip as 'close the seven open functions'; the audit says the seven are ONE of THREE independent blockers, and the other two were never in the order. Run the whole audit before any lane is dispatched at this TU again -- it costs three commands and it changes the objective's size by an order of magnitude.

BLOCKER 1 -- FOUR OF THE SEVEN ARE COUNT-ASYMMETRIC, so no postprocessor rule can ever serve them (claim.law.webfrank-cannot-close-a-count-asymmetric-residual.20260831.v1) and they must close at SOURCE. Measured with `python tools/gdl/fndiff.py game/enemy/enemy.c <fn> --ops`. Count-symmetric, hence rule-eligible: do_enemy_move T905/O905 (`target-only: +1 addi +1 lwz  ours-only: -2 fmr`); damage_enemy T571/O571 (`target-only: +1 b +1 bgt  ours-only: -1 beq -1 cror`); move_logic00 T244/O244, multiset IDENTICAL, 53 differing words all REGFIELD-ONLY. Count-asymmetric: move_logic10 T1085/O1087 (`ours-only: -2 fmr`); generate_enemy T242/O241 (`target-only: +1 mr`); move_logic22 T227/O228 (`ours-only: -1 mr`); fn_80046680 T117/O118 (`ours-only: -1 mr`). THREE OF THOSE FOUR ARE ONE FAMILY the corpus has already closed as source-unreachable: fn_80046680 and move_logic22 both pay an ADDR16_LO home copy (the target forms a file-scope address directly into its home register, ours routes the low half through a scratch and copies), and fn_80046680 is NAMED IN THE P ROSTER of claim.law.addrlo-home-copy-class-is-general-temp-and-shadow-coupled.20260901.v1 (40 functions over 2983 paired, S = 0 in 953 opportunities); move_logic22 carries the identical shape with a VOLATILE home (r4), which is why that census -- counting only callee-saved homes -- did not list it. claim.law.addr16-lo-address-homed-via-r0-is-source-unreachable.20260831.v2 measured TWELVE candidate discriminants across the same census and all twelve fail to separate the population, with a working positive control proving the search could have found a real one. generate_enemy pays the same copy in the OTHER direction (target-only `mr`), the direction claim.law.dead-local-identity-reuse-also-closes-ours-only-home-copies.20260831.v1 explicitly scopes as source-unreachable once the dead-carrier enumeration is empty -- and this run measured that enumeration empty by NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL proof (attempt.EN_generate-enemy-...20260904.v1).

BLOCKER 2 -- THE TU'S .text IS MISORDERED, WHICH NO SCORE SEES. `python tools/gdl/textorder.py game/enemy/enemy.c` exits 1 and prints `MISORDERED game/enemy/enemy (62 shared .text functions, 0 target-only, 4 ours-only)`, with a single group-1 divergence beginning at position 4 that runs the length of the TU. The target opens `EnemyWorldDamage fn_80046140 fn_8004646C fn_80046680 do_ai move_logic00 ...` and ends `... check_enemy_pos gendir_8004FBC8 find_enemy_slot`; ours opens `fn_80046140 fn_8004CFAC fn_8004D030 fn_8004DB3C fn_8004E448 update_enemy_milestone adjust_msidx enemy_update check_vacancy do_ai move_logic00 ...` and ends `... fn_8004D958 fn_8004646C fn_80046680`. Roughly twenty functions are in the wrong place, including four that the order's own roster calls open. The fix is SOURCE-DEFINITION ORDER in the .c and no score confirms it, so it must be done and then re-screened with the same command. Not compared, and therefore also unresolved: four ours-only symbols `enemy_bss_order`, `EnemyMovingAwayFromBirth`, `fabsf_`, `update_vel`.

BLOCKER 3 -- THREE DATA SECTIONS ARE UNCLAIMED. `python tools/gdl/datadiff.py game/enemy/enemy.c --sections` exits 1 with `3 blocker(s)`: `.data: SIZE target 0x0 vs ours 0x190`, `.sdata2: SIZE target 0x0 vs ours 0x10C`, `.bss: SIZE target 0x0 vs ours 0x678C`, each flagged `OURS is LARGER than the target -- the DOL-range byte check is structurally blind to this`. The target side reads 0x0 because the split has no data claim for this TU. This is PRE-EXISTING, not caused by this lane's three commits: the pass-opening `defake_gate.py baseline game/enemy/enemy.c --at-head` at 0f4151839 already stamped `DATA baseline: 4 non-text section(s), 0/1120 matched bytes ... .data 0/0; .sdata2 0/0; extab 0/448; extabindex 0/672`. The TU additionally carries 1120 bytes of LINK-level exception tables (extab 448 B at 74.5575%, extabindex 672 B) that any instruction-count change relocates.

CONSEQUENCE, stated so the next order does not re-derive it. game/enemy/enemy.c is not one lane's work and it is not seven closes. It needs, in this order: the .text source-definition reorder (mechanical, unscored, must be re-screened with textorder.py); data claims for three sections; and then four source closes that today sit behind the best-evidenced source-unreachable result in the corpus. An order that actually wants this flip should first attack the ADDR16_LO home-copy class image-wide, where the payoff is 40+ functions rather than two, because until that class breaks the TU cannot flip no matter how much work lands inside it.
